column1: Large full-library AEM Sites publishing jobs wedge after concurrent Oak commit conflicts
column6:
Customer problem: Full-library AEM Sites outputs for large libraries failed or remained in Post-Publishing for many hours. One wedged job blocked later jobs in Waiting. Cancel remained at cancellationRequested=true. Single-topic and small-map output continued to work.

Observed evidence: DITA-OT reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Author logs recorded javax.jcr.InvalidItemStateException with OakState0002 conflicting concurrent change in PublishWorkflowGenerationAEMSiteRenditionStep.publishDITATopicList while rendered pages were being committed to Oak. Multiple full-library runs targeted overlapping output paths. No heap/OOM, 429-rate-limit, or OutputJob NPE was observed in the captured window.

Recovery history: Engineering-approved cleanup terminated wedged workflow state and removed correlated stale output-history/job-manager nodes for two affected libraries. Support later reported fresh output generation running normally for those libraries. Four additional library jobs were still reported for follow-up when the Jira was closed.

Evidence boundary: OakState0002 concurrent-write collision is an evidenced trigger in this incident, not proof that every stuck Post-Publishing job has the same root cause. Map Dashboard versus global Publish Dashboard state inconsistency was also observed. Official product documentation did not define automatic Oak-conflict recovery, same-path serialization, retry budget, or operator cleanup procedure.
column17: Evidenced incident trigger: concurrent full-library AEM Sites generations wrote overlapping rendered-page paths and hit OakState0002 / InvalidItemStateException during the post-DITA-OT JCR commit stage. DITA-OT generation itself completed successfully. This is not an exclusive product-wide root-cause claim; dashboard/history-state inconsistency and other historical stuck-queue incidents can have different causes.
column18:
Historical recovery validation: correlate map UUID and job ID before any cleanup; use engineering approval; inventory and back up exact nodes; preserve sibling and unrelated jobs; retain audit evidence and rollback; verify dashboards, workflow terminal state, queue draining, fresh publish, and absence of orphan state.

Temporary operational mitigation until a product safeguard is implemented: run full-library AEM Sites generations sequentially for the same or overlapping output destination. This is incident-derived guidance, not documented product behavior or an approved permanent contract.

Proposed permanent-safeguard tests: concurrent overlapping publishes must complete successfully with valid page count, links, assets, metadata, and no duplicate/partial/orphan pages; retry exhaustion must reach a bounded terminal failure with an actionable error; cancel of stale/untracked jobs must not remain indefinitely in cancellation-requested state; one wedged job must not block unrelated destinations; Map and global dashboards must agree. Exact locking, retry, serialization, cleanup, and source-of-truth implementation remain engineering decisions.

Performance boundary: approximately two-hour normal and nine-hour degraded customer timings are observations only, not hard pass/fail thresholds without an approved controlled benchmark.
